top.title: Mike McCarthy responds to Aaron Rodgers leaking Packers cheer in Steelers game: ‘Embarrassing moment’
top.description: Mike McCarthy responds to Aaron Rodgers leaking Packers cheer in Steelers game: ‘Embarrassing moment’ originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers officially released quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, following an appearance that Rodgers made on ESPN that was anything but boring. During an interview with ESPN's Pat McAfee , Rodgers called head coach Mike McCarthy "unhealthy" and rattled off hordes of reasons he was unhappy with the coach. Rodgers even claimed that McCarthy fell asleep during team meetings and missing walk-throughs. "Last Thursday, I was in a quarterback meeting and in 10 minutes I heard snoring," Rodgers said. "Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he misses walk-through... Saturday, he misses the team meeting." One of the craziest accusations was that McCarthy led a "‘1, 2, 3, Packers " chant during the Steelers' game against the Eagles . NFL insider Jordan Schultz says this is true , and McCarthy was asked about it during a presser on Wednesday. Mike McCarthy reacts to Aaron Rodgers' accusations of a Green Bay Packers cheer during a Pittsburgh Steelers game When asked about that accusation of the chant, McCarthy responded and seemed to admit it happened. "The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional," McCarthy said, according to USA Today . "There's conversations prior to that. Embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments." He added, "Aaron and I have a long history. He has a lot of opinions, and those are things we always talked about. Once again, I consider those private conversations." McCarthy also confirmed that Pittsburgh released Rodgers during that presser. Now, Rodgers is a free agent, and he'll either take that as a sign to officially retire to land elsewhere. top.title: Bruno Fernandes weighs in on Senne Lammens errors after Man United drop Champions League points
top.description: Bruno Fernandes scored twice as Manchester United drew 2-2 with Sporting CP -Credit:Gualter Fatia - UEFA, UEFA via Getty Images Bruno Fernandes reassured Senne Lammens that "mistakes are part of football" following the goalkeeper's two costly errors against Sporting Lisbon in the UEFA Champions League. Lammens conceded a penalty in the first half, charging out of his area to bring down Sporting defender Maximiliano Araújo, before fumbling a cross to gift the home side their equalizer in the 80th minute. United appeared set to snatch victory when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira bundled the ball into his own net, only for VAR to disallow the goal after Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have fouled him. Alejandro Garnacho casts doubt over Aston Villa future after taking drastic action Tim Weah won't 'beg' for USMNT return after Mauricio Pochettino snubbed Marseille captain -Credit:PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA, AFP via Getty Images "I think we started the game very well," Fernandes told TNT Sports, via the Manchester Evening News . "Then we gave up the way we set it up. We were in full control of the game with the ball very well. We gave one or two counters, but we were very good in recovering the positions. "Then they get the goal. I think we were still in control of the game, probably not creating as much as we wanted. We didn't have enough people in the last third. We arrived with only one or two players, that was difficult. "Then in the second half we get the two goals and I think there was the moment where we should have pushed a little bit more and it was the other way around. We sit a little bit. We were a little bit afraid of the moment also probably and we end up conceding another goal." Asked about Lammens' mistakes, he said: "It's part of football. Mistakes are part of football and from that you get goals, but obviously it's not an individual sport, so everyone has to take the blame for everything we do good and everything we do bad. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "So I think the main thing and the most important thing is that we understand that we need to be in this together in the good and in the bad moments and it's not going to change the belief we have in each other." Fernandes also revealed that Mauricio Pochettino urged his players to push further forward following the first half. "He wanted more aggression, more bodies up front, more runs," said Fernandes. "I think the first goal comes from that, I mean, it comes from a run from behind. We said the run from the second line was important for us because they couldn't catch that. "They have a very high line. It was difficult for the front players to get onside. So from the second line, me, Youri [Tielemans], we should have done a little bit more. We did it in the first half at spells, but not enough. In the second half, we started doing it more, and we created a lot of danger, and it led to the two goals for us."

top.title: Scorned AD reportedly suing Michigan despite getting over $17 million for not working
top.description: Credit: Vasha Hunt-Imagn Images On Tuesday, the University of Michigan announced that, despite earlier reports that it had landed on Trev Alberts as its next athletic director, the university would not be proceeding with the hire. “The University of Michigan’s search for its next athletic director is ongoing,” Michigan spokesperson Paul Corliss said in a statement. “As we navigate a rapidly changing landscape in intercollegiate athletics, the values that define Michigan will guide our decisions and reinforce our commitment to excellence and integrity, both in the classroom and in competition.” The decision was reportedly made after the school’s regents became aware of Alberts’ answers during a deposition during his tenure as the AD for the University of Nebraska. Former Nebraska Cornhuskers women’s basketball player Ashley Scoggin sued the Nebraska Board of Regents, the women’s basketball coach, and then-AD Trev Alberts in February 2024, after she was dismissed from the team due to a sexual relationship with assistant coach Chuck Love. During a deposition with Scoggin’s lawyers, Alberts was asked if it was permissible for students and coaches to be involved sexually and answered, in part, that “it just depends.” Alberts’ answer likely held more weight with Michigan’s brass than it would with other schools due to its former head coach, Sherrone Moore, being fired for cause after it was determined that he had an inappropriate sexual relationship with a football staffer. All the same, following Michigan’s decision not to hire him after learning about his answer, Alberts is now suing, according to The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman. “Trev Alberts plans to file a lawsuit against the University of Michigan and perhaps incoming president C. Cybele Raver after the university rescinded his job offer earlier this week, his attorney Tom Mars told @TheAthletic,” Feldman reported. Alberts response is somewhat surprising, considering that reports indicate that he signed a MOU with Michigan last week that will ensure he gets paid over $17 million despite his offer being rescinded, as well as the multi-million amount that he owes Texas A&M for departing the school, with which he held the same role. top.title: Unpacking every crazy moment from Sporting-Man United
top.description: Three penalties, two disallowed goals, one fluke, and a “main-character energy” referee: Manchester United ’s 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League had a bit of everything. Mauricio Pochettino was denied his first win as United manager as his side saw a late winner disallowed by VAR in a bonkers clash in Lisbon. Referee Szymon Marciniak was in the thick of the action throughout and in the 84th minute ruled that Patrick Dorgu had fouled Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, who let a corner from Bruno Fernandes slip through his fingers. But that was not all - here’s a breakdown of all the main incidents from a crazy night. 32’ Man United concede two penalties in three minutes (SPO 1-0 MUN) After a subdued start in Lisbon, Mauricio Pochettino saw his new defence implode as they conceded two penalties in the space of three minutes. The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg. If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Senne Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left. But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box. Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row. It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season. And Lammens went from hero to zero as he undid his penalty save by quickly conceding another. (SPO 1-0 MUN) Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled that Youri Tielemans had committed a foul on Goncalo Inacio when he slid to poke the ball through to Amad Diallo, who headed into an empty net at the second attempt after the goalkeeper deflected his shot onto the crossbar. However, because Marciniak had already blown his whistle to stop play following the challenge from Tielemans, VAR could not intervene. Tielemans did not appear to commit a foul and instead won the ball fairly against Inacio when he went to ground to play the ball through to Amad. top.title: "Now isn't the time" - Kompany avoids finger pointing as Bayern suffer first defeat
top.description: "Now isn't the time" - Kompany avoids finger pointing as Bayern suffer first defeat On the 18th attempt, Bayern Munich suffered their first defeat of the campaign on Wednesday, with Lille securing a 2-1 win in the Champions League. Making the trip to northern France, Vincent Kompany's depleted side took the lead via Dayot Upamecano in the 15th minute, and strolled into half-time carrying a deserved 1-0 lead. But, the hosts would flip the clash on its head in the second half, with Ayase Ueda's equaliser followed by an own-goal from Aleksandar Pavlovic just minutes later, condemning Der Rekordmeister to their first defeat since April. Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, boss Kompany reflected on what was most definitely a tale of two halves. “The first half was pretty much how we'd envisioned our game would go,” said the Belgian, after his side strutted their stuff with relative ease despite operating with a depleted 11. "It highlighted both our strengths and our weaknesses. But overall, it was a good first half. "In the second half, we just couldn't find our rhythm anymore, And then, of course, you don't have that breathing room, that space where you're so far ahead that the game is already decided. That's part of football. Of course, you have to play the game until the very end. “We tried. So, that's that, there's no blame to be placed on anyone, but the second goal, of course, shouldn't have happened," he added, referencing Pavlovic's own goal in which the midfielder will not want to see again when analysing the defeat. However, the Bayern boss insisted that the blame game is far from the right path to take in this instance. “From experience, I know these moments. I know that now isn't the time; we have to fight for our chances, stick together, fight for it and enjoy the battle; that's part of it." With the club reviving the ‘FC Hollywood’ tag as a result of recent events, Kompany has the task of steadying the ship as the winter break approaches, and with a trip to Hamburg coming at the weekend, the German champions will be looking for a response to their first loss of the season, potentially easing the tension surrounding the club at this moment in time.

top.title: A Toothpaste Marketer Turned an Energy Drink Into Two F1 Teams Valued at $8.65 Billion
top.description: Red Bull’s founder Dietrich Mateschitz went from marketing toothpaste to owning two F1 teams that Sportico now values at a combined $8.65 billion. It started with a case of jet lag. Mateschitz, who worked in marketing for the German consumer-goods company Blendax, bought a bottle of a Thai tonic called Krating Daeng on the way from Bangkok airport into the city. “One glass and the jet lag was gone,” he later recalled, according to Wikipedia’s account of his life . From a Thai Tonic to a Grand Prix Grid In 1984, he and the drink’s Thai creator, Chaleo Yoovidhya, each put in $500,000 to start Red Bull, with 49% apiece. Red Bull launched in Austria in 1987. Formula 1 came next. Ford sold him its struggling Jaguar team in November 2004, reportedly for a single dollar. BBC Sport reported at the time that Ford wanted a symbolic dollar and a commitment to invest $400 million in the team over three seasons. It raced as Red Bull Racing from 2005. A second team followed in September 2005, when Mateschitz and Gerhard Berger bought Minardi. It became Toro Rosso in 2006, and today it races as Racing Bulls. Sebastian Vettel’s Toro Rosso at Monza in 2008, the year he won there. Image Credit: Jane Belinda Smith / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) Winning With the Junior Team First The little team scored the first big payoff. Sebastian Vettel took Toro Rosso to victory at Monza in 2008, on a wet day, and was promoted to the senior team soon after. Red Bull Racing has since won six constructors’ championships, in 2010 to 2013 and in 2022 and 2023, and eight drivers’ titles: four for Vettel from 2010 to 2013 and four for Max Verstappen from 2021 to 2024. The money has kept pace. In its November 2026 rankings, Sportico values Red Bull at $5.6 billion, fourth among the 11 teams and up 30% on a year ago. It puts Racing Bulls at $3.05 billion, up 49%. Together, that makes $8.65 billion for a business that began with a pair of $500,000 checks. Mateschitz died in October 2022, but both teams are still part of the company he built.

top.title: Bayern Munich stunned 2-1 by Lille in Champions League after second half collapse
top.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images It’s all gone from bad to worse for Bayern Munich as the German Rekordmeister fell to a 2-1 loss to Lille in France in the Champions League. The result comes just a few short days after the disappointing 1-1 draw with FC Köln in the Bundeslig a, a match in which Bayern lost both Harry Kane and Michael Olise to injury in the first half, with Kane facing a long spell on the sidelines. Against Lille, Vincent Kompany started an attacking four of Lennart Karl, Tom Bischof, Nathaniel Brown, and Konrad Laimer. He really didn’t have many other options with Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, and Ismael Saibari all out injured, and both Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz starting on the bench after returning from lengthy injury layoffs. Bayern looked to be in control of the match even with an injury-hit squad, taking a 1-0 lead into halftime on a Dayot Upamecano header off a Bischof corner. Konrad Laimer missed a gilt-edged chance to make it 2-0 for the Bundesliga champions, leaving Bayern with a narrow lead at the break despite controlling 60% of possession and putting at least five shots on target. In the second half, Lille dealt Bayern a one-two sucker punch in the 62nd and 65th minutes, scoring through Ayase Ueda and an unfortunate own goal from Aleksandar Pavlović as he tried to clear a shot that had come off the post. The midfielder falling to his knees and burying his face in his palms captured Bayern’s frustration on a night when the club conceded twice in three minutes and left Lille empty-handed. Speaking after the match, Laimer offered his assessment and said Bayern lost too much of the control and momentum it had in the first 45 minutes. “I thought we had a very decent first half, in which we implemented many of the things we had set out to do. I think we were very aggressive, had good energy, won a lot of duels, and picked up a lot of second balls. But we lost a bit of that in the second half. Then we conceded two goals, and things became far too easy for them. We also failed to produce the level of performance we are capable of. And now we’re standing here with zero points,” the Austr ian said (via @iMiaSanMia ). Bayern now finds itself in 15th place in the Champions League table, needing results to climb back into the top eight for automatic knockout-stage qualification. With its next two matches in the competition coming against Slavia Prague and a struggling Manchester United squad, Bayern should have a chance to turn things around—though nothing is guaranteed. That’s the nature of the Champions League, a point Laimer underscored. “That’s Champions League football. That’s how it is. Now it’s simply about recovering quickly because we’re going through a very intense period with very little time between games,” he stressed. Join the conversation! top.title: How Does Gabe Vincent Signing Impact the Kings?
top.description: On Sunday, Nov. 22, the Sacramento Kings signed veteran point guard Gabe Vincent to a one-year, non-guaranteed deal. The move comes after it became increasingly apparent that Malik Monk was not cutting it as a backup point guard. The Kings have played Monk less and less as the season has progressed because their offense is poor with him on the floor. Vincent slotting into the Kings’ lineup as backup point guard shifts Monk to a secondary ball-handling role, where he has been more comfortable in the past. He also provides continuity behind rookie Darius Acuff Jr. , a player the organization sees as their superstar of the future. Vincent is a Savvy Player Acuff is third in the NBA in minutes per game, averaging 36.6. It is unprecedented for a rookie to lead that category, but the coaching staff has deemed it necessary to play him so much. With Acuff off the floor, turnovers increase, offensive possessions stall, and players take poor shots. Vincent represents stability; he makes wise decisions with the ball. His numbers don’t jump off the stat sheet — Vincent averaged just 3.9 points, 1.6 assists, and 1.1 rebounds in 13.3 minutes per game. What does stand out, however, is his minuscule 0.6 turnovers per game. The 1.6-to-0.6 assist-to-turnover ratio means he averages 2.67 assists for every singular turnover. Monk’s ratio is 3.6-to-1.69, meaning he averages 2.11 assists before turning the ball over. Vincent doesn’t play himself off the floor; he does what the coaching staff asks of him in his minutes. One could categorize his play style as boring, but Kings fans would much prefer boring over unpredictable. At this point in his career, Gabe Vincent does exactly one thing well: handle the ball without turning it over. A perfectly safe, boring, dependable ball-handler. The Kings have clearly had enough of the Monk backup PG experience and opted for his exact opposite. https://t.co/fkJsWbAGrB — Jack Dann (@JackBDann) November 22, 2026 Looking beyond his offensive impact, Vincent is not a liability on defense. When engaged, he’s a solid point-of-attack defender who plays with hustle and physicality. Monk is lack-luster defensively, so Vincent has a leg up on him there. Even if Vincent’s shot isn’t falling on a given night, he can ensure the second unit doesn’t completely lose the game. Vincent Provides Mentorship Vincent’s journey to the NBA was anything but easy. After completing his college career at UC Santa Barbara, Vincent entered the NBA Draft, but went undrafted. He wound up playing for his hometown Stockton Kings in the NBA G League. top.title: Joe Burrow 'certainly' surprised by Steelers' release of Aaron Rodgers
top.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said Nov. 25 that he thinks the Pittsburgh Steelers' release of future Pro Football Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers was unexpected, but didn't say much else about it. "I don't know much about the situation," Burrow said . "Certainly surprising, but I guess I don't know much." Burrow was asked whether it could be good for the Bengals' playoff hopes that Rodgers was released. "I don't know," Burrow said. "We'll see." About one hour earlier, the Steelers announced they released Rodgers during what's believed to be his 22nd and final NFL season after a very public rift with head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow met on the field after Cincinnati's 38-18 rout of Pittsburgh on NBC's Sunday Night Football. "That was a clinic out there, kid," Rodgers told Burrow as they shook hands. "Good job, keep rolling." "Thank you, bro," Burrow responded. "If this is your last one, much love and respect." In a postgame interview on the field with Melissa Stark, Burrow talked about his respect for Rodgers. "I just have a lot of respect for him and what he's done," Burrow said . "He's such a good player and continues to play at a high level at 40-whatever he is," Burrow told reporters . "Somebody that I loved watching growing up. Really second to none as far as throwing the football and really still is. Just have a lot of appreciation for what he's brought to the game and all the things that he's done." Burrow was unable to break a record held by Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning during the team's NFL Week 11 loss to the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium. Burrow finished the game with two touchdowns. He was seeking a sixth straight game with at least four passing/rushing TDs. Burrow enters the Bengals' NFL Week 12 game against the New Orleans Saints needing one touchdown pass to match Boomer Esiason for third place in Bengals' franchise history. top.title: Isak 'in a good place' as Liverpool close on Champions League last 16
top.description: Alexander Isak scored twice in Liverpool's 3-0 win over Club Brugge (NICOLAS TUCAT) Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz fired Liverpool towards the Champions League last 16 with an impressive 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday. Both star forwards struggled to justify their price tags during a difficult first season, but are beginning to show why they cost nearly a combined £250 million ($327 million) to bring them to Anfield last year. Isak's cool finish opened the scoring and the Swede then rounded off a fine night for Andoni Iraola's men with his 10th goal of the season. Moments earlier Wirtz had netted for the fifth consecutive game for club and country with a sublime finish. "Perfect away win, I would say," Isak told TNT Sports. "I'm in a good place and the team is in a good place, most importantly. Hopefully, it gets better from here. "The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in, we have a dangerous attack. It feels good." Victory takes Liverpool up to fifth in the Champions League table and closing in on a top-eight finish that will secure a place in the last 16. "An important game for us at a key moment in the group stage," said Iraola. "It puts us in a good position, guarantees qualification for the knockout stage, but now we want to go to the top eight." Brugge began the night level on points with the six-time European champions, but failed to score for the first time in 38 games to slip down to 13th. Liverpool were able to cruise to a 4-0 win over Manchester United with a man advantage for over 80 minutes at the weekend. But Iraola still took the chance to rest captain Virgil van Dijk, Alexis Mac Allister and teenage sensation Rio Ngumoha with one eye on Sunday's Merseyside derby at Everton. - Sommer error opens door - Brugge's experienced goalkeeper Yann Sommer handed Liverpool the breakthrough when his poor pass was pounced on by Bradley Barcola, who teed up Dominik Szoboszlai to cross for Isak to tap in the opener on 13 minutes. Ngumoha was forced into action before half-time after Victor Munoz hobbled off in the only setback of the night for Liverpool. Sommer made amends with a brilliant stop to deny Szoboszlai as Liverpool pressed to double their advantage after the break. The second goal arrived 11 minutes from time when Ngumoha wriggled free to tee up Wirtz on the edge of the box. Wirtz has credited former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp for helping him to find top form during the international break with Germany. His newfound confidence was on show as he curled a fine strike in off the inside of the post to end any hope of a Brugge revival. Isak then pounced on a long punt forward by Alisson Becker to spring in behind the Belgians' defence and delicately lift the ball over Sommer as Liverpool made amends for a shock defeat to Fenerbahce last time out in the Champions League. kca/mw

top.title: QB Rodgers released by Steelers after slamming coach McCarthy
top.description: FILE PHOTO - A view of the NFL logo on the pitch before the 2026 NFL Game between Atalanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at the Santiago Bernabéu. (is associated with: «QB Rodgers released by Steelers after slamming coach McCarthy») Nathalia Araújo/dpa The Pittsburgh Steelers have waived Aaron Rodgers after the quarterback slammed coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday. Rodgers was benched ahead of the NFL game against the Denver Broncos on Friday and said during The Pat McAfeee Show that he wouldn't return to the team. "That ship has sailed," Rodgers said of his time with the Steelers. He explained that he found out from team-mate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched in favour of Mason Rudolph, and that he still hasn't heard the news from McCarthy. He then went on to recount that McCarthy was "snoring" in team meetings and that what happened this week was not "abnormal." "Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened," Rodgers said. He added that the issues with the coach go back to training camp during summer and revealed that McCarthy broke down the team at half-time of their 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles last Sunday with "one, two, three, Packers." "And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at half-time, towards the end of it (...) And there's some rambling or something, and without even a heads-up, he says, 'All right, one, two, three, (Green Bay) Packers.'" Since Rodgers' release happened after the league's trade deadline, he's available to be claimed by any other team on waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he will become an unrestricted free agent. The quarterback won the Super Bowl in 2011 with the Packers - back then coached by McCarthy - and was named the NFL most valuable player four times (2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021). McCarthy took the Steelers coaching job this year after Mike Tomlin resigned following 19 seasons in the position.

top.title: PSG's perfect Champions League record ends as Roma snatch 2-2 draw with late penalty
top.description: Donyell Malen's 78th-minute penalty earned Roma a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday, ending the defending champions' perfect record in this season's Champions League. The result also halted PSG's 12-game winning streak in all competitions, leaving Real Madrid as the only team with a 100% record after five league-phase matches.

top.title: Bill Simmons reveals how he would react if New England Patriots sign Aaron Rodgers
top.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ career with the Pittsburgh Steelers is over. But there is still a possibility he plays in the NFL again. After an explosive interview attacking Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers has been waived by the team. There will now be an opportunity for quarterback-needy NFL teams to negotiate with Rodgers and bring him in to try and save their season. One of these could be the New England Patriots, who have just lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to a fractured ankle. Patriots fan Bill Simmons said he would ultimately welcome a move. He wrote on X: “Just so you know — if the Pats signed Rodgers I’d talk myself into it before our turkey is carved tomorrow.” Options for Rodgers The New England Patriots are currently planning to start Tommy DeVito for the rest of the season, which does not fill many fans with a lot of confidence. Another option could be for Rodgers to sign for the Steelers’ rivals the Baltimore Ravens, who are set to play Pittsburgh twice still. The Ravens have lost six straight games and recently traded for Jacoby Brissett, but Rodgers could be an upgrade. A further option could be the New York Giants, if they believe he can be an instant upgrade on JJ McCarthy. But it is still unclear if Rodgers wants to play again, after a dramatic 24 hours. top.description: “But I thought we had possession… how did they score?” LILLE, FRANCE - (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images FC Krankenhaus is so back. Bayern Munich does not have an attack at the moment. Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Manuel Neuer did not feature in this game. This team has more starters injured than available. Without an attack, the game was set for an undesirable outcome. But holy smokes, this was even below expectations. All defenders, no defending Bayern Munich fielded all but one available starting-calibre defender in Jonathan Tah. No less than 6 defenders started this game, which would’ve made one believe in a solid defensive outcome. Surprise surprise, we don’t do that here. Defence continues to be Bayern’s Achilles heel. One could argue that the key lies in balance, but unfortunately, Vincent Kompany’s hands were tied. It was simply not possible to field a sensible starting XI today, and the result, though unsurprising, still managed to disappoint. This team is still bang average bad at dealing with set pieces and a total shambles when facing counterattacks. A bit like if a fox is released into a chicken coop. Lille had one game plan: through balls and lobbed balls and runners behind the defence. And it worked to perfection. We are in 2026, and counter-attacks continue to be Bayern’s kryptonite. That and Josip Stanišić. A headless octopus That is what the team looked like tonight. Too much passing (yes, such a thing exists) and a lack of meaningful chance creation, coupled with zero execution. Lennart Karl might as well have taken a vacation. Aside from Alpine Zidane (also known as the Energizer Bunny) Konrad Laimer, who has four lungs and runs twice the total distance of the next player, the rest of the squad looked checked out. Is this an acceptance of defeat? Does the team not believe it is worth fighting? Or perhaps it is simply the fact that a bunch of midfielders cannot be expected to shoulder any sort of attacking responsibility. They did what they were perhaps accustomed to doing: passing. Some failed at that too. Jonas Urbig is one player who can walk away from this game with his head held high… he really is the next sweeper keeper. He just doesn’t have the right support from his teammates at the moment. This is about to be a rough stretch for Bayern fans. Meister of the Match: The Corner Flag? top.title: Vincent Kompany says Bayern Munich lost rhythm in 2-1 loss to LOSC Lille
top.description: Photo by Getty Images | ﻿Photo by Getty Images Bayern Munich created chaos for the first 45 minutes in the Champions League clash against Lille. Dayot Upamecano scored a header from a well-designed set piece an d gave Bayern a lead heading into the locker room at halftime. In the second half, Bayern made sloppy passes, reacted too slowly in defensive situations, and ultimately ran out of steam and ideas against the French side. In the postgame interview (via @iMiaSanMia ), Bayern manager Vincent Kompany analyzed the tale of two halves. “The first half was definitely very much what we had envisaged for this game,” said Kompany. “We showed our strengths, but also some of our weaknesses. Overall, though, it was a good first half. Then, in the second half, we simply couldn’t get back into our rhythm. And naturally, that means you no longer have the same fre edom and space to play as well as you would like and see the game through comfortably.” Kompany insisted, “That’s part of football, of course. You have to play your game right until the final minute. We tried. It’s not a question of energy or anything like that, and there are no accusations in that regard. The second goal, of course, should never have happened. But as I said, I know these situations from ex perience. I know what this means now. We have to fight to regain our momentum. Stick together, fight, and even enjoy that battle a little. That’s part of it.” Bayern will need to be more consistent for the final month of 2026. The competition is not very forgiving, and now that Lille has proven Bayern is beatable, opponents will play with an extra burst of energy to pull off an upset of their own. Join the conversation! top.title: Ex-Brewers pitcher lands contract with Padres
top.description: Orlando Ramirez-Imagn Images Ex-Brewers pitcher lands contract with Padres appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Diego Padres have reportedly agreed to a contract with relief pitcher JoJo Romero in MLB free agency. Jeff Passan initially reported the news , while Ken Rosenthal provided details on the contract itself. “Free-agent lefty reliever JoJo Romero in agreement with Padres on three-year, $21 million contract, source tells @TheAthletic,” Rosenthal reported. Star left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon is currently a free agent . Reports have said that Morejon is generating plenty of interest from teams around the sport. A Morejon reunion remains possible for the Padres, but it is far from guaranteed to happen. At the very least, Romero provides San Diego with a veteran left-handed option out of the bullpen. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Romero, 30, has pitched in the big leagues since 2020. He spent 2026 with the St. Louis Cardinals and Milwaukee Brewers. The left-hander ultimately recorded a respectable 3.36 ERA across 55 total outings between his time in Milwaukee and St. Louis. Romero has quietly been a steady reliever over the years. He’s turned in an ERA of 3.68 or better in each season since 2023. From 2024-2026, Romero made at least 55 or more starts. He is not necessarily a lights out reliever who is going to completely dominate opponents (although he did have a stellar 2025 campaign that saw him turn in a 2.07 ERA in 65 outings) but he is reliable overall. The Padres’ signing of JoJo Romero may be overlooked by some, but this move will likely prove to be crucial during the 2027 MLB season. It will be especially pivotal if Adrian Morejon ends up signing with another ball club. top.title: Injuries required BYU’s offense to often reinvent itself — and it’s still No. 10 in the country
top.description: BYU running back LJ Martin, left, runs into TCU linebacker Hudson Hooper (37) during game Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026, in Fort Worth, Texas. | LM Otero, Associated Press Wake Forest leapfrogged BYU in the College Football Playoff poll released Tuesday night, a development that should surprise absolutely no one who has been paying attention to the sport the past few weeks, maybe the past few years. The Demon Deacons (10-1) jumped three spots to No. 8 after walloping coaching-depleted Georgia Tech, while BYU (9-2) held steady at No. 10 after scratching past an inspired Kansas team 31-29 in triple overtime. Wake Forest has been punishing opponents — albeit weaker opponents — while BYU has bided its time while waiting for a bunch of players to get healthy and back on the field. Clearly, the committee is now paying attention to style points , the so-called “eye test,” and margin of victory, and not just metrics that, in this particular head-to-head comparison of BYU and Wake Forest, would seemingly favor the Cougars. So what can BYU do about that? Obviously, coach Kalani Sitake’s Cougars need to keep winning; a loss against Cincinnati (6-5, 3-5) on Saturday at LaVell Edwards Stadium (1:30 p.m. MST, Fox) would be one of the most devastating setbacks in program history. They also need to show more explosiveness on offense, which should be more attainable now that their best player, running back LJ Martin , is closer to 100% and also because Cincinnati does not have one of the better defenses in the Big 12. The Bearcats are No. 135 in total defense (453.8 yards per game) and No. 117 in scoring defense (30.6 points per game). They are slightly better against the run (104th) than against the pass (136th), but have been vulnerable to both. It is time for BYU to make some hay. Offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said Tuesday that, personnel-wise, the Cougars are almost back to where they were when the season started; second-string RB Sione Moa remains out, but tight end Roger Saleapaga and starting right tackle Andrew Gentry are getting closer to returning. All the shuffling, especially the absence and then less-than-full-strength return of Martin, has caused Roderick to have to reinvent the offense multiple times this season. It is an offense that — despite being a respectable No. 45 in scoring (30.7) and No. 62 in total offense (387.9) — hasn’t really found its true identity in 2026. “Yeah, that’s a really good observation,” Roderick said. “We spent seven games (going) week to week. ‘Who can play this week? top.title: Depleted Bayern beaten by Lille in Champions League
top.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was forced to improvise due to a wave of injuries. (Francois LO PRESTI) Bayern Munich suffered their first defeat of the season on Wednesday, losing 2-1 at Lille in the Champions League as a tough week for the German giants worsened. Dayot Upamecano opened the scoring for Bayern but Ayase Ueda levelled for Lille before a horror Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal gifted the hosts victory. Bayern were the only club in Europe's top-five leagues yet to have lost a match in any competition this season but came unstuck against a Lille side who entered the game second last in the table. The defeat continued a terrible past few days for Bayern, who lost star striker Harry Kane for several months to a serious ankle injury on Friday and then had Michael Olise ruled out with a foot complaint. Coach Vincent Kompany, who himself returned this week after a month out with meningeal irritation, brought Jamal Musiala off the bench for the last 15 minutes. Musiala has found himself in the headlines this week after several members of Bayern's hierarchy called for the 23-year-old to take a pay cut as he battles his way back from a neurological condition, drawing fierce condemnation from players' unions. "I know these moments from experience," Kompany said to DAZN. "I know what this is like. Now, we have to fight to create our own moments. "We need to stick together, fight, and even learn to enjoy the struggle -- that's all part of it. "There are no excuses. It's simply the reality we face, and we have to stand together." The defeat in France left Bayern 15th in the Champions League table with three games remaining, while Lille's first win moved them to within two points of the knockout places. "This game didn't decide the Champions League," Kompany said. "PSG didn't even reach the top eight in the last two years and remember they won the Champions League back-to-back." - Karl fills in up front - Bayern's forward line included just one recognised forward in 18-year-old winger Lennart Karl. The 1.68-metre tall Karl led the attack, with Kompany naming three defenders behind him. Bayern centre-back Upamecano, a striker in his youth, on Tuesday laughed off suggestions he may play up front despite scoring in two of his past four Bundesliga games. But with 15 minutes gone, the France defender channeled the injured Kane when he rose high to head in Bayern's opener from a Tom Bischof corner. Bayern controlled the game until half-time but were fortunate when VAR intervened to disallow a Ueda goal early in the second half for a foul on Joshua Kimmich. The Japan striker did not have to wait long to get on the scoresheet though. Just after the hour mark, Ueda guided a Nathan Ngoy pass across goal and into the bottom corner. top.title: Missing Out on Dylan Larkin Might Not Be Such a Bad Thing for the Minnesota Wild
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As much as I would have loved to see Dylan Larkin in a Minnesota Wild jersey, I can’t blame general manager Bill Guerin if he wasn’t willing to give up what the Montreal Canadiens did to get him. The Canadiens sent Kirby Dach, Michael Hage, Samuel Montembeault and four draft picks , including two conditional first-rounders, to the Detroit Red Wings on Sunday in exchange for Larkin and two draft picks. Larkin is signed through the 2030-31 season at an $8.7 million cap hit, so it’s understandable why Montreal was willing to give up so much for him. But how much do the Wild really need to add to its lineup to win a Stanley Cup? The Wild already have two fantastic offensive players on the wings in Kirill Kaprizov and Matt Boldy, and Joel Eriksson Ek is one of the better two-way centers in the NHL. Another good center could be enough to put this team over the top. TSN’s Pierre LeBrun has brought up three names Bill Guerin could turn his attention to after missing out on Larkin: Ryan O’Reilly, Pavel Zacha and Evgeni Malkin. All three could become unrestricted free agents next summer. Ryan O’Reilly Would Be a Great Fit in Minnesota If I’m Guerin, O’Reilly is the guy I’m calling about. He’s spent most of his career playing against some of the best players in the NHL, he’s great in the faceoff circle and he can still produce offensively. He won the Stanley Cup, Conn Smythe Trophy and Selke Trophy with the St. Louis Blues in 2019. Imagine being an opposing coach trying to get your best players away from Eriksson Ek in a playoff series, only to have them end up on the ice against O’Reilly. The Wild would be a miserable team to play against. Getting him out of Nashville might be easier said than done, though. O’Reilly doesn’t have any trade protection in his contract, but LeBrun reported that he doesn’t want to leave Nashville. He also had an agreement with former Predators general manager Barry Trotz that any potential trades would be discussed with him beforehand. We’ll have to see whether Chris MacFarland handles things the same way. If O’Reilly is open to a move, Minnesota should be all over him. Pavel Zacha Could Be More Than a Rental What I like about Zacha is that there’s a chance he could be part of the Wild’s plans beyond this season. He’s considerably younger than O’Reilly and Malkin, and his ability to play both center and wing gives the Wild some options with its lineup. He’s not Larkin, but how much offense do they really need him to create on his own if he’s playing with Kaprizov or Boldy? He’s a big, skilled forward who could do quite well playing with either of them. Zacha has partial trade protection, and there’s no guarantee the Boston Bruins will even want to move him. The team’s fourth coach since the 1969 season, McCarthy is a break from Steelers tradition, as he has previous coaching experience. Rodgers was even part of the process to bring McCarthy to the Steelers. "Rodgers said he suggested general manager Omar Khan consider McCarthy as a candidate for the Steelers' head coach opening early in the offseason, but he wasn't sure how seriously his former head coach would be considered," ESPN's Brooke Pryor previously reported. "I encouraged him for an outside perspective to interview Mike," Rodgers said, per Pryor. nigeria.description: Donyell Malen’s penalty gave Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the injury-hit reigning champions saw their perfect record in this season’s competition come to an end. Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute on a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, giving Roma a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out. Roma had earlier taken the lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to equalise before substitute Ousmane Dembele put PSG briefly in front with a penalty of his own. The result ends PSG’s perfect record in this season’s league phase, and halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team. They fall two points behind Real Madrid, who are now clear at the top of the standings as the only side still with a 100 percent record after five matches. It is only a minor setback for PSG in their quest to finish in the top eight of the 36-team table, and therefore qualify directly for the last 16 without having to go through the play-off round like in the last two campaigns. But the Parisians could have done with the boost of a victory as they come to terms with the loss of the outstanding Desire Doue, who may not play again this season after rupturing the ACL in his right knee last weekend. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, another of their outstanding attacking players, recently succumbed to the same injury, while Dembele has been struggling for fitness too and PSG’s prospects of winning a third straight Champions League title are undoubtedly diminished as a result. Dembele’s presence on the bench at kick-off meant that none of PSG’s five top scorers from last season were in their line-up here, with the others either injured or having departed in the case of Bradley Barcola and Goncalo Ramos. Meanwhile, Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini raised eyebrows by leaving Malen out of his starting XI. The Dutchman is running at an average of more than a goal a game this season and netted four against Parma last weekend. – Dembele spot-kick – However, Roma have been in prolific form in general, netting 26 goals in their last seven matches before arriving in the French capital. They went ahead inside five minutes here as Matias Soule cut the ball back from the byline and Spanish defender Hermoso was on hand to convert. Roma had blown even more promising leads already this season, though, losing 4-3 at home to Real Madrid after leading 3-1 with eight minutes left, and then going down 3-2 at Old Trafford despite being 2-0 ahead at half-time. nigeria.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
nigeria.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. nigeria.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. nigeria.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
nigeria.description: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028 Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets. The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF. With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement. Exchanges only with partners that qualify Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security. Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange. The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year. The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said. Down from 74 partners The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027. Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses. The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month. In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29. Bithumb breach ran for 15 days Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there. That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks. Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected. Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers. It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken. For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets. Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. entertainment.description: The fifth edition of Entertainment Week Africa brought together filmmakers, musicians, designers, artists, tech founders, investors, mentors, policymakers and fans for six days of screenings, showcases, masterclasses and celebrations under the theme Five Years of Closing the Gap . People from 121 countries and territories applied to speak, attend or screen their work, and more than 19,000 people joined the programme in person and online, as EWA streamed its sessions live for the first time. Over the six days, more than 150 speakers led nearly 100 panels, masterclasses, workshops, roundtables and podcast sessions, while around 50 films were screened across the week. The celebrations began on Opening Night at the Livespot Entertarium, where guests were treated to an evening of music, fashion, film and comedy to mark five years of EWA. Sixteen emerging artists performed in front of a room of industry leaders, creatives and partners, and the night featured an exclusive 30-minute screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios , written by Dami Elebe and executive produced by Deola Art Alade . By day, EbonyLife Place hosted a packed programme across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Art & Animation; Live Events & Production; and Creative Enterprise. Nissi Ogulu led a masterclass on animation as Africa’s next big storytelling frontier, and From Lagos to Disney explored what it takes to bring African stories to global screens. Creators picked up practical tips in sessions with Victoire, Ifeoma Udeme and Canva. Other sessions tackled sync licensing, music funding, building Africa’s touring circuit and turning creative skills into businesses. The podcast stage kept the energy going with live recordings of CreativiTea and Crea8torium , which closed the final day. Fashion took over the Entertarium for The Runway Coterie, an evening of bold collections that ended with the announcement of the EWA Fashion Lab winners after a week-long programme with mentors. Hooked By Lade won first place with ₦2 million, Estaz took second place and ₦1 million, and Melira placed third, winning ₦500,000. Lush Hair styled the runway as the show’s hair sponsor. Next door, the EWA Art Floor invited guests into The Spaces Between Us , an exhibition that blended photography, painting, installation, archival work, fashion and live performance. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg. Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row. sports.title: "Now isn't the time" - Kompany avoids finger pointing as Bayern suffer first defeat
sports.description: "Now isn't the time" - Kompany avoids finger pointing as Bayern suffer first defeat On the 18th attempt, Bayern Munich suffered their first defeat of the campaign on Wednesday, with Lille securing a 2-1 win in the Champions League. Making the trip to northern France, Vincent Kompany's depleted side took the lead via Dayot Upamecano in the 15th minute, and strolled into half-time carrying a deserved 1-0 lead. But, the hosts would flip the clash on its head in the second half, with Ayase Ueda's equaliser followed by an own-goal from Aleksandar Pavlovic just minutes later, condemning Der Rekordmeister to their first defeat since April. Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, boss Kompany reflected on what was most definitely a tale of two halves. “The first half was pretty much how we'd envisioned our game would go,” said the Belgian, after his side strutted their stuff with relative ease despite operating with a depleted 11. "It highlighted both our strengths and our weaknesses. But overall, it was a good first half. "In the second half, we just couldn't find our rhythm anymore, And then, of course, you don't have that breathing room, that space where you're so far ahead that the game is already decided. That's part of football. Of course, you have to play the game until the very end. “We tried. So, that's that, there's no blame to be placed on anyone, but the second goal, of course, shouldn't have happened," he added, referencing Pavlovic's own goal in which the midfielder will not want to see again when analysing the defeat. However, the Bayern boss insisted that the blame game is far from the right path to take in this instance. “From experience, I know these moments. I know that now isn't the time; we have to fight for our chances, stick together, fight for it and enjoy the battle; that's part of it." With the club reviving the ‘FC Hollywood’ tag as a result of recent events, Kompany has the task of steadying the ship as the winter break approaches, and with a trip to Hamburg coming at the weekend, the German champions will be looking for a response to their first loss of the season, potentially easing the tension surrounding the club at this moment in time.

sports.title: A Toothpaste Marketer Turned an Energy Drink Into Two F1 Teams Valued at $8.65 Billion
sports.description: Red Bull’s founder Dietrich Mateschitz went from marketing toothpaste to owning two F1 teams that Sportico now values at a combined $8.65 billion. It started with a case of jet lag. Mateschitz, who worked in marketing for the German consumer-goods company Blendax, bought a bottle of a Thai tonic called Krating Daeng on the way from Bangkok airport into the city. “One glass and the jet lag was gone,” he later recalled, according to Wikipedia’s account of his life . From a Thai Tonic to a Grand Prix Grid In 1984, he and the drink’s Thai creator, Chaleo Yoovidhya, each put in $500,000 to start Red Bull, with 49% apiece. Red Bull launched in Austria in 1987. Formula 1 came next. Ford sold him its struggling Jaguar team in November 2004, reportedly for a single dollar. BBC Sport reported at the time that Ford wanted a symbolic dollar and a commitment to invest $400 million in the team over three seasons. It raced as Red Bull Racing from 2005. A second team followed in September 2005, when Mateschitz and Gerhard Berger bought Minardi. It became Toro Rosso in 2006, and today it races as Racing Bulls. Sebastian Vettel’s Toro Rosso at Monza in 2008, the year he won there. Image Credit: Jane Belinda Smith / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) Winning With the Junior Team First The little team scored the first big payoff. Sebastian Vettel took Toro Rosso to victory at Monza in 2008, on a wet day, and was promoted to the senior team soon after. Red Bull Racing has since won six constructors’ championships, in 2010 to 2013 and in 2022 and 2023, and eight drivers’ titles: four for Vettel from 2010 to 2013 and four for Max Verstappen from 2021 to 2024. The money has kept pace. In its November 2026 rankings, Sportico values Red Bull at $5.6 billion, fourth among the 11 teams and up 30% on a year ago. It puts Racing Bulls at $3.05 billion, up 49%. Together, that makes $8.65 billion for a business that began with a pair of $500,000 checks. Mateschitz died in October 2022, but both teams are still part of the company he built.

sports.title: Bayern Munich stunned 2-1 by Lille in Champions League after second half collapse
sports.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images It’s all gone from bad to worse for Bayern Munich as the German Rekordmeister fell to a 2-1 loss to Lille in France in the Champions League. The result comes just a few short days after the disappointing 1-1 draw with FC Köln in the Bundeslig a, a match in which Bayern lost both Harry Kane and Michael Olise to injury in the first half, with Kane facing a long spell on the sidelines. Against Lille, Vincent Kompany started an attacking four of Lennart Karl, Tom Bischof, Nathaniel Brown, and Konrad Laimer. He really didn’t have many other options with Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, and Ismael Saibari all out injured, and both Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz starting on the bench after returning from lengthy injury layoffs. Bayern looked to be in control of the match even with an injury-hit squad, taking a 1-0 lead into halftime on a Dayot Upamecano header off a Bischof corner. Konrad Laimer missed a gilt-edged chance to make it 2-0 for the Bundesliga champions, leaving Bayern with a narrow lead at the break despite controlling 60% of possession and putting at least five shots on target. In the second half, Lille dealt Bayern a one-two sucker punch in the 62nd and 65th minutes, scoring through Ayase Ueda and an unfortunate own goal from Aleksandar Pavlović as he tried to clear a shot that had come off the post. The midfielder falling to his knees and burying his face in his palms captured Bayern’s frustration on a night when the club conceded twice in three minutes and left Lille empty-handed. Speaking after the match, Laimer offered his assessment and said Bayern lost too much of the control and momentum it had in the first 45 minutes. “I thought we had a very decent first half, in which we implemented many of the things we had set out to do. I think we were very aggressive, had good energy, won a lot of duels, and picked up a lot of second balls. But we lost a bit of that in the second half. Then we conceded two goals, and things became far too easy for them. We also failed to produce the level of performance we are capable of. And now we’re standing here with zero points,” the Austr ian said (via @iMiaSanMia ). Bayern now finds itself in 15th place in the Champions League table, needing results to climb back into the top eight for automatic knockout-stage qualification. With its next two matches in the competition coming against Slavia Prague and a struggling Manchester United squad, Bayern should have a chance to turn things around—though nothing is guaranteed. That’s the nature of the Champions League, a point Laimer underscored. “That’s Champions League football. That’s how it is. sports.title: How Does Gabe Vincent Signing Impact the Kings?
sports.description: On Sunday, Nov. 22, the Sacramento Kings signed veteran point guard Gabe Vincent to a one-year, non-guaranteed deal. The move comes after it became increasingly apparent that Malik Monk was not cutting it as a backup point guard. The Kings have played Monk less and less as the season has progressed because their offense is poor with him on the floor. Vincent slotting into the Kings’ lineup as backup point guard shifts Monk to a secondary ball-handling role, where he has been more comfortable in the past. He also provides continuity behind rookie Darius Acuff Jr. , a player the organization sees as their superstar of the future. Vincent is a Savvy Player Acuff is third in the NBA in minutes per game, averaging 36.6. It is unprecedented for a rookie to lead that category, but the coaching staff has deemed it necessary to play him so much. With Acuff off the floor, turnovers increase, offensive possessions stall, and players take poor shots. Vincent represents stability; he makes wise decisions with the ball. His numbers don’t jump off the stat sheet — Vincent averaged just 3.9 points, 1.6 assists, and 1.1 rebounds in 13.3 minutes per game. What does stand out, however, is his minuscule 0.6 turnovers per game. The 1.6-to-0.6 assist-to-turnover ratio means he averages 2.67 assists for every singular turnover. sports.title: Joe Burrow 'certainly' surprised by Steelers' release of Aaron Rodgers
sports.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said Nov. 25 that he thinks the Pittsburgh Steelers' release of future Pro Football Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers was unexpected, but didn't say much else about it. "I don't know much about the situation," Burrow said . "Certainly surprising, but I guess I don't know much." Burrow was asked whether it could be good for the Bengals' playoff hopes that Rodgers was released. "I don't know," Burrow said. "We'll see." About one hour earlier, the Steelers announced they released Rodgers during what's believed to be his 22nd and final NFL season after a very public rift with head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow met on the field after Cincinnati's 38-18 rout of Pittsburgh on NBC's Sunday Night Football. "That was a clinic out there, kid," Rodgers told Burrow as they shook hands. "Good job, keep rolling." "Thank you, bro," Burrow responded. "If this is your last one, much love and respect." In a postgame interview on the field with Melissa Stark, Burrow talked about his respect for Rodgers. "I just have a lot of respect for him and what he's done," Burrow said . "He's such a good player and continues to play at a high level at 40-whatever he is," Burrow told reporters . "Somebody that I loved watching growing up. Really second to none as far as throwing the football and really still is. Just have a lot of appreciation for what he's brought to the game and all the things that he's done." Burrow was unable to break a record held by Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning during the team's NFL Week 11 loss to the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium. Burrow finished the game with two touchdowns. He was seeking a sixth straight game with at least four passing/rushing TDs. Burrow enters the Bengals' NFL Week 12 game against the New Orleans Saints needing one touchdown pass to match Boomer Esiason for third place in Bengals' franchise history.
